Subject: Asteria Bank — activation SLA & per-tenant warm pool ask

Team,

Quick context: Asteria (CIO Claire Donovan) is asking for a deterministic activation SLA for production traffic as a condition of signing — specifically they want 95th/99th tail guarantees for their tenant during business hours (sub-100ms for text generation in our hosted/dedicated hybrid). They are worried about variability when their tenant gets cold and have asked if we can provide a per-tenant warm pool or some form of resident affinity to avoid cold starts.

Attached: Asteria_MVP_SOW.pdf and a draft mutual action plan (MAP-2026Q4.xlsx).

As this is part of a >$1M TCV deal (AST-3729), I need a concise feasibility summary:
- Minimal viable approach we can offer in Q4 that materially reduces cold-start tail latency
- Key tradeoffs (cost, isolation, billing model, operational burden)
- Rough effort estimate and proposed rollout gating (canary vs full launch)
- Any blockers that would require legal/pricing exceptions

Desired: short write-up by EOD Thursday (10/29) so I can share a concrete MAP with Claire on Monday. If we think this needs an engineering spike, flag it and estimate spike hours.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30 if helpful.

—Markus

Subject: Re: Asteria Bank — activation SLA & per-tenant warm pool ask

Markus,

High level technical take: there are three feasible paths, ordered by implementation effort and cost impact:

1) Tenant warm pool (MVP): pre-warm a small set of inference workers pinned to Asteria during business hours. Pros: predictable tail, fast. Cons: extra reserved capacity per tenant, fragmentation of GPU utilization, billing/commit changes. Estimated baseline build: 2w infra + 1w runtime + 1w integration/tests (about 4w engineering across infra and runtime).

2) KV-cache/affinity pinning: keep larger shared nodes but persist tenant KV-caches to speed up hot-paths; reduces cold-attention penalty but less deterministic than dedicated warm pool. Lower cost delta, lower tail improvement. 2w engineering to instrument cache pinning + 1w perf testing.

3) Model residency (dedicated model variant pinned to tenant): heavier — requires scheduler changes and capacity commitments, ~6-8w. Best tail but highest cost.

Blocking/unknowns:
- Billing model: need pricing addendum for reserved warm capacity for this tenant.
- Autoscaler behavior: current autoscaler will reclaim nodes under cluster pressure unless we mark them reserved; requires autoscaler changes.
- Observability: need SLA probes at route-level to validate tail improvements — add 1w for dashboarding/alerts.

I spun up an initial design doc and attached some notes. I recommend we scope an MVP focused on option (1) but with telemetry hooks to measure end-to-end impact, and option (2) as a lower-cost fallback. If product wants to aim for a Q4 pilot, engineering can commit to a 3-week spike to produce a PoC and an ETA.

Next step: create JIRA ticket to track scope (ENG-4932).

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks for the quick responses. A few product considerations to shape scope: 

- MVP definition: expose a per-tenant setting (Console flag) for "reserved warm pool" that maps to a minimal reserved instance footprint (e.g., N workers per tenant) and is billable as a monthly reservation. We should provide an SLA during business hours only to limit exposure.
- Acceptance criteria: demonstrable 95th/99th reduction in tail latency (benchmark before/after), ability to failover to shared nodes automatically, and billing line-item in invoices.
- Rollout: pilot with Asteria as canary for 6 weeks. If pilot meets SLA and stability targets, offer as add-on for other enterprise customers.

Risks/asks:
- Legal/pricing: need a short pricing addendum and Ops runbook for capacity reservation. Can Sales/Finance route this to Legal?
- Product telemetry: Jordan, agree that we need a week of dashboards/alerts to validate.
- CS work: Marissa, please prepare a success plan and runbook for Asteria including escalation points.

Timeline proposal: 3-week engineering spike starting Nov 2 → lightweight PoC + perf tests → 3-week pilot setup & validation = 6w total. If Sales needs an earlier MAP, we can shrink spike to 1w but pilot risk increases.

I linked the HubSpot deal so we can align on acceptance criteria: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/AST-3729

Monica
Monica Patel
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Claire,

Per our call, thanks again for flagging the activation SLA requirement. Internally we've sketched an MVP to address the tail-latency risk: a per-tenant reserved warm pool (Console toggle) that guarantees a small number of pre-warmed workers during your defined business hours. Product & Eng propose a 6-week pilot: 1) 2–3 week engineering spike to stand up pilot; 2) 3-week pilot window; 3) post-pilot validation.

What we need from you to finalize the MAP:
- Sign-off on pilot acceptance criteria (95th/99th target reductions) — see attached MAP-2026Q4.xlsx (section: acceptance_criteria).
- Confirmation you can commit to minimum reserved capacity for the pilot (we'll propose numbers in the next 48h).
- Procurement contact for a short pricing addendum (we'll need to list the monthly delta for reserved capacity).

If this all looks reasonable I will kick off the internal spike and route the pricing note to Legal once we have estimated capacity.

Appended below is the short internal note Jordan sent with feasibility options.

—Markus
